punchline: Cirque du Soleil beat the circus business by dropping the animals and borrowing from theatre.
thirty_sec: In 1984, a group of street performers in Quebec started Cirque du Soleil while the circus business was shrinking. They dropped the animal acts and star performers, and borrowed story, music and dance from theatre. Their audience was adults, with tickets priced well above any ordinary circus. The book says that in under twenty years it reached the revenue Ringling Bros. had needed more than a century to build.
